item.title: How a 'tropical' shortcut could help particle collider experiments
item.description: Particle accelerators are expensive. Not just to build or to run, but also to predict the outcome of measurements obtained from them.

item.title: Are we about to solve the greatest mystery of the neutrino?
item.description: We have long had a seemingly simple question about neutrinos: how much do they weigh? Now, a gigantic experiment in China is poised to find out – and the answer could transform particle physics forever

item.title: Will we observe dark matter as a particle or a wave?
item.description: We have arguably already discovered dark matter, says columnist Chanda Prescod-Weinstein. To observe it, we will need to figure out whether we expect it to act like a particle or a wave.

item.title: A single antimatter particle was held in a trap for months
item.description: After trapping a positron for the first time, physicists plan to use the resulting data to look for answers to one of particle physics’ biggest questions

item.title: New research shows a neutrino laser is impossible
item.description: Due to physical and fundamental limitations, an earlier proposal for producing laserlike beams of neutrinos cannot be achieved, scientists report.

item.title: How an MIT graduate student helped a team of young scientists test their experiment at CERN
item.description: Physics PhD student Manu Srivastava helped high school students in India develop a test that could contribute to one of the world’s largest neutrino experiments.

item.title: On the hunt for dark matter
item.description: From Broadway to MIT’s Laboratory for Nuclear Science, PhD student Jessica Fry doesn’t do anything halfway. Now she’s hunting for the universe’s most elusive particle.
